label: FY2027 Q1 (Jul–Sep 2026)
asOf: close of $1,330.05 on 29 Oct 2026, $1,305 after hours (5:45 pm ET, StockAnalysis)
headline: 85% gross margin and profits still rising, yet the stock is 40% off its high: the market is pricing the top of the memory cycle

points.t: The longer AI inference runs, the more context it has to store. Datacenter is now about half of industry bits, and Sandisk's datacenter revenue grew about 18x in a year.

points.b: Customers lock in supply with long contracts
points.t: NBM contracts cover half of FY27 and two-thirds of FY28 bits, 95% with investment-grade customers; the pipeline exceeds supply through 2030.
$5.0B of buybacks this quarter while capex is just 3.4% of revenue; no extra capacity, bit growth stays in the teens.

reaction: Stock: closed at $1,330.05 (−5.3%) in the session before the report; after hours it rose, then fell to $1,305 (−1.9%). Revenue, EPS and next-quarter guidance all beat, yet the stock is about 43% below its 52-week high of $2,354.39. The same day Intel cut its next-quarter guidance (mainly PCs, according to an analyst on the call), and the first question was about memory prices hurting PCs; management said PC and phone units fall this year, but storage per device still rises next year. Consensus from Benzinga: EPS $46.36, revenue $10.70B. The next day (10/30) it closed at $1,150.89 (−13.5%), turning the small after-hours dip into a steep fall.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: Almost all growth came from datacenter and edge; consumer is shrinking because of higher prices. The company is steering more output to datacenter customers.

rows.why: Only $0.27B a year ago. Customers include three US hyperscalers; the QLC product (internal name Stargate) is qualified and ramping. TLC to QLC is about 70:30. Management says its datacenter share is still below the industry's (about half of bits) and will keep closing the gap in 2027.

Phones, PCs, cars, IoT. Premium and mainstream demand is steady, the low end is shrinking; auto and IoT are growing fast. Management expects PC units to dip again next year, but total storage to grow.
Memory cards, USB drives, portable drives. Management says “the market is adjusting to higher pricing”, in other words consumers are being priced out.

segments.note: Revenue rose 23% quarter on quarter, about 60% from volume and 40% from price (last quarter it was about one-third volume, two-thirds price). Q2 guidance still includes “modest” price increases.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Sandisk sells the “memory” of AI inference. Its 85% gross margin is the extra cost paid by cloud, PC and phone makers; its long contracts and prepayments also lock those customers into years of spending.

items.w: Each generated token looks back at the context before it (the KV cache). What doesn't fit in GPU memory goes to flash, which is cheaper than recomputing. Management estimates datacenter rose from about 20% of industry bits early this decade to about half; datacenter bit demand grows another ~40% in 2027, and KV cache will be about one-third of the AI datacenter flash market by 2030.

NBM contracts include committed volumes, minimum financial guarantees and pricing mechanisms. 95% of NBM customers are investment grade, with about $130B of combined annual operating cash flow. Most guarantees are bank-issued and off Sandisk's balance sheet; direct prepayments were $1.94B last quarter and $0.47B this quarter.

items.b: Its margin is someone else's cost
items.w: A year ago gross margin was 30%. The same week, Microsoft said its capex includes higher memory and storage prices, Amazon listed “supply volatility, including for memory chips” as a risk, and Intel cut guidance on PC demand. Sandisk's own consumer business fell 29% q/q. How long prices hold depends on what customers can absorb.

Capex was $0.38B this quarter, mid-single digits of revenue for the year; bit output keeps growing in the mid-to-high teens, and node transitions won't be sped up to chase demand. Spare cash goes to buybacks: $5.0B this quarter. Supply discipline is what keeps prices up.

Profits rise every quarter, yet the stock is about 40% below its 52-week high. At about 6.5x next-twelve-month consensus, it carries the classic multiple of a cyclical memory company at peak earnings: the market is betting that price increases will end.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: The company's own long-term model actually assumes margins come down: gross margin back to about 80% from 85% today. So the question is not how much higher prices go, but how much profit the long contracts protect once they stop rising.

items.w: The fabs shared with Kioxia move through nodes on a fixed plan, so bit output grows in the mid-to-high teens a year. A wafer takes about 120 days, so supply can't be reallocated quickly. Demand (datacenter +40%) is growing well ahead of supply.

The CFO said prices will keep rising modestly through the year. A new variable is SLC: some customers want to run NAND in high-endurance SLC mode to replace part of DRAM. One SLC bit uses the capacity of 3–4 TLC/QLC bits, so wide adoption would tighten the market further.
HBF aims for near-HBM read bandwidth with far more capacity; the first die has taped out. The company says HBF is not in its long-term model, and its size won't be known until customers test samples.

The August Investor Day model for FY2028–2030: revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens, non-GAAP gross margin about 80%, operating margin about 75%, adjusted free cash flow margin about 50%, and 100% of excess cash returned. Today's 85% gross and 80% operating margins are already above that model.

Memory has always cycled through price rises, capacity additions, glut and price cuts. Signals to watch: peers' capex and expansion plans; whether contract prices turn down; how much consumer and PC demand is crushed by prices; and whether cloud capex financing tightens. NBMs lock in volume, but how their pricing works in a downturn has not been disclosed.

trends.why: Almost 5x in five quarters; Q2 guide adds another 12%
About 18x in a year, 44% of revenue
From 30% to 85%, above the long-term model

valuation.take: Cheap on any current measure: about 11x trailing earnings, under 6x on annualized Q2 guidance, about a 9% free cash flow yield. It is cheap because the market doesn't believe these profits last: once memory prices fall, today's earnings are the peak.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: FY2028 profits
scenarios.sub: Jul 2027–Jun 2028, starting from FY27 revenue of about $49.2B
head: Case

scenarios.note: The base case follows the Investor Day long-term model: revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens and gross margin around 80%. The bear case assumes memory prices fall, revenue drops by a third and gross margin returns to 55% (its late-2025 level); the bull case assumes price rises and SLC demand continue. Opex 5–6% of revenue, 14.3% tax, 142–150M shares (pre-split, after buybacks). Multiples: in a downturn memory profits thin out and P/E rises, so the bear case gets 9x; base and bull get 7.5–8x, slightly above today's 6.5x because long contracts reduce volatility. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY28 EPS × our multiple; pre-split prices (divide by 8 after 20 Nov)
pricezone.why: Today's price is near the top of the zone: buying now, the base case gains about 41% and the bear case loses about 39%, so reward and risk are about even. Lower in the zone the bear-case loss shrinks: buying at $950, the bear case loses only about 15% while the base case nearly doubles. The zone is wide because memory stocks swing hard; waiting for an exact price makes little sense.
pricezone.note: After the split (from 20 Nov): bear about $101, base about $234, bull about $308, zone about $119–163.

history.title: Against its own history
history.sub: Forward P/E (next-twelve-month consensus) at quarter ends; spun off in Feb 2025, so only 6 quarter ends
history.note: About 6.5x now, below every quarter end since listing. The multiple keeps shrinking not because the stock is slow, but because profits are rising much faster than the price: the market only pays a low multiple for “peak earnings”. StockAnalysis data; current value uses pre-report consensus.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.note: Operating cash flow was $6.36B and capex $54M (gross capex including the joint-venture fabs about $0.38B). Receivables rose $1.88B in the quarter, which the CFO put down to customer mix. Taxes paid on vested employee stock were $0.76B, far more than a year ago because the stock has risen so much.

changes.before: 8 customers on NBMs, covering half of FY27 and two-thirds of FY28 bits.
changes.now: Final share “likely higher than current levels”; the largest customer signed a second tranche, and customers say they underestimated how much flash they need.

changes.before: Only said AI drives structural demand growth.
changes.now: Datacenter over 55% of the 2027 market with bit demand up about 40%; PC, phone and datacenter bit demand all grow.

changes.before: Talked mainly about TLC and QLC.
changes.now: Customers are discussing running NAND in SLC mode to replace some DRAM for endurance; management says it's “early” but would tighten the market.
Announced an 8-for-1 split to make the employee stock plan easier to join; keeps returning “100% of excess cash” and has no plan to borrow for buybacks.
